I just wanted to weigh in on the Game Day Threads and open up the conversation once again, and after this week I feel like it deserves a fresh discussion.

I fear that they Game Day Threads in their current form are a waste of time.

I don't say this in a cynical sense mind you, but from the view of true time management. Since we don't necessarily have access to a bot, I'm constantly reminded that "someone" needs to put in a lot of work, and I'm quickly realizing that, despite my best intentions, I'm an inebriated mess by 4:00pm most Sundays. I really want to be a helpful mod and not just a title holder, so I'll approach this like I approach my job irl - observations, ideas, and solutions. So here we go:

Observations:

  1. I don't think we are presently large enough of a subverse to properly utilize Game Day Threads - or at least not how we use them. Considering where we came from (reddit), the level of engagement in the actual thread has been very underwhelming, considering...

  2. ...We are averaging about 15-20 comments each week on those GDTs. As you likely remember, on reddit it's common to see 600 - 2000 comments on a GDT, and those are for individual games. I know the reason (see 3), but the fact remains that the work that goes into them is disproportionate to the amount they are used. I genuinely fear those of you who have been vigilantly updating threads are detracting from you personal fun of Sunday by updating a thread that's scantly used.

  3. The irc has been an absolute blast, and it's where most contributors seem to gravitate. Here in our first year together, and not having any idea what the future holds, I think this is our money-maker and the feature that will build a stronger community. For the record, I think people are interacting exceedingly civil, and it's fun to watch people learn the personalities of participants.

  4. Due to its relative popularity and general ease of use, the irc is effectively dissuading people from remaining at the GDT. Particularly in light of voat's volatility between checking bits and slow-to-process comments, you're almost a minute behind on everything if you remain in the comments.

Ideas:

  1. Continue to create a GDT thread for all games at each time slot, but remove the need for constant updates.

  2. No more than three lines of info for each game (reduce clutter and need for updates): match-up and location, link to ESPN (or other site that will keep a box score updated), and maybe link to a stream if available.

  3. IF anybody really wants it, maybe include a line for score, but keep it basic. Personally, I recommend NOT doing this, but that's just my take.

  4. At the top of the post, heavily promote the irc, and maybe include a quick FAQ link or something for using the irc in case some have never used it because they are old(ish) and not as computer savvy (kind of like me). (*this is my favorite idea)

  5. In case I missed it above, keep grouping games together by time slot, but make all three of them at the beginning of Sunday, post them in the morning, and just sticky the applicable time slot roughly an hour or so before game-time.

Solutions?

Up to the group. I really do want to apologize if I seem like I haven't been pulling my weight recently. I certainly don't want to be "that guy," and I was only really put on the team to work the Team Subverse Subscription Drive. That isn't to say I haven't been enjoying the mod side of the sub, it's just that I'll be the first one to admit that I'm not as strong with computer use. I'm happy to help in other ways, but I also want to make sure you guys aren't feeling burned out engaging in a practice that might not be completely worth the effort for the time being, or at least in its current form.

Let me know what you guys think, and I'll be happy to help out however I can.

-CS
